q: Arrhenius's concept of acids and bases is applicable in the case of ____ of acids and bases.
e: Arrhenius's concept of acids and bases is applicable in the case of ionisation of acids and bases. Arrhenius acids give H+ in water and Arrhenius bases give OH- in water.

q: In an aqueous solution, strong acids and bases are almost completely dissociated (ionised), producing hydrogen ions ($H^+$) and ____ ions.
e: In an aqueous solution, strong acids and bases are almost completely dissociated (ionised), producing hydrogen ions (H+) and hydroxide ions. A strong acid ionises completely in water, so almost every molecule dumps its proton.

q: When dealing with aqueous solutions of weak acids or bases, however, more information about the system is required as they undergo ____ dissociation.
e: When dealing with aqueous solutions of weak acids or bases, however, more information about the system is required as they undergo partial dissociation. A weak acid ionises only partly in water, so most of its molecules stay undissociated.

q: The strengths of acids and bases can be ranked by the ____ to which they ionise in aqueous solutions.
e: The strengths of acids and bases can be ranked by the extent to which they ionise in aqueous solutions. Extent is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Strong acids are strong electrolytes that ____ ionise in water.
e: Strong acids are strong electrolytes that completely ionise in water. A strong acid ionises completely in water, so almost every molecule dumps its proton.

q: Most of the strong acids are ____ acids.
e: Most of the strong acids are inorganic acids. A strong acid ionises completely in water, so almost every molecule dumps its proton.

q: Weak acids are weak electrolytes that partially ionise only to a ____ extent in water.
e: Weak acids are weak electrolytes that partially ionise only to a limited extent in water. A weak acid ionises only partly in water, so most of its molecules stay undissociated.

q: The ____ of an acid may be defined as the number of $H^+$ ions that one molecule of acid can produce.
e: The basicity of an acid may be defined as the number of H+ ions that one molecule of acid can produce. Basicity is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called ____ acids, diprotic acids, or triprotic acids, respectively.
e: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called monoprotic acids, diprotic acids, or triprotic acids, respectively. Monoprotic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called monoprotic acids, ____ acids, or triprotic acids, respectively.
e: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called monoprotic acids, diprotic acids, or triprotic acids, respectively. Diprotic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called monoprotic acids, diprotic acids, or ____ acids, respectively.
e: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called monoprotic acids, diprotic acids, or triprotic acids, respectively. Triprotic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A base is a substance that reacts with an acid whereas an alkali is a base that is ____ in water.
e: A base is a substance that reacts with an acid whereas an alkali is a base that is soluble in water. Soluble is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Hydroxides of alkali metals (Li, Na, K) and certain ____ metals (Ca, Sr, Ba) are strong bases.
e: Hydroxides of alkali metals (Li, Na, K) and certain alkaline earth metals (Ca, Sr, Ba) are strong bases. A strong base ionises completely in water and produces a high [OH-].

q: Like strong acids, strong bases are strong electrolytes that ionise ____ in water.
e: Like strong acids, strong bases are strong electrolytes that ionise completely in water. A strong base ionises completely in water and produces a high [OH-].

q: Weak bases, like weak acids, are weak electrolytes that ionise to a very ____ extent in water.
e: Weak bases, like weak acids, are weak electrolytes that ionise to a very limited extent in water. A weak base ionises only a little in water.

q: The ____ of a base is measured by the number of molecules of a monoprotic acid, like HCl, which will neutralise one molecule of the base.
e: The acidity of a base is measured by the number of molecules of a monoprotic acid, like HCl, which will neutralise one molecule of the base. Acidity is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The relative strengths of acids may be determined by measuring the acid ionisation constants, ____, in aqueous solutions.
e: The relative strengths of acids may be determined by measuring the acid ionisation constants, Ka, in aqueous solutions. Ka is the acid dissociation constant; a larger Ka means a stronger weak acid.

q: The strength of an acid is related to its degree of ionisation, the magnitude of which is reflected by the value of its ____, $K_a$.
e: The strength of an acid is related to its degree of ionisation, the magnitude of which is reflected by the value of its dissociation constant, Ka. Ka is the acid dissociation constant; a larger Ka means a stronger weak acid.

q: The larger the $K_a$ value of an acid, the greater its dissociation, the higher the concentrations of $H^+$ and the ____ is the acid.
e: The larger the Ka value of an acid, the greater its dissociation, the higher the concentrations of H+ and the stronger is the acid. Ka is the acid dissociation constant; a larger Ka means a stronger weak acid.

q: The dissociation constant of a weak acid is sometimes expressed on a ____ scale, which for acid is denoted by the relation $pK_a = -\log K_a$.
e: The dissociation constant of a weak acid is sometimes expressed on a logarithmic scale, which for acid is denoted by the relation pKa = - Ka. A weak acid ionises only partly in water, so most of its molecules stay undissociated.

q: Small $K_a$ values (corresponding to large $pK_a$) indicate ____ acids.
e: Small Ka values (corresponding to large pKa) indicate weak acids. Ka is the acid dissociation constant; a larger Ka means a stronger weak acid.

q: The higher the $K_b$ value of a base, the greater its dissociation and the higher the concentrations of ____ ions will be.
e: The higher the Kb value of a base, the greater its dissociation and the higher the concentrations of OH- ions will be. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.

q: The water is not included in the equilibrium expression as it is in such ____, that the concentration of water does not change significantly with changes in the concentrations of other species.
e: The water is not included in the equilibrium expression as it is in such great excess, that the concentration of water does not change significantly with changes in the concentrations of other species. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: For a base, the dissociation constant is expressed on a logarithmic scale, which is denoted by the relation $pK_b = $ ____.
e: For a base, the dissociation constant is expressed on a logarithmic scale, which is denoted by the relation pKb = -Kb. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.

q: Small $K_b$ values (corresponding to large $pK_b$) indicate ____ bases.
e: Small Kb values (corresponding to large pKb) indicate weak bases. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.
